Class StringUtils

java.lang.Object
io.github.ericmedvet.jnb.datastructure.StringUtils
public class StringUtils extends Object
This class consist of static utility methods for operating with strings or producing strings.

  • Method Details

    • collapse

      public static String collapse(String string)
      Collapses a given string string into an acronym. The method splits the string by the predefined regex "[.\u2192\\[\\]]+" and then extracts the first alphanumeric character from each resulting piece to form the acronym.
      Parameters:
      string - the string to be collapsed
      Returns:
      the collapsed acronym string

    • formatSize

      public static int formatSize(String format)
      Estimates the formatted size of a string based on a given format string. This method attempts to format various types (int, double, LocalDateTime, and string) with the provided format and returns the length of the resulting string.
      Parameters:
      format - the format string to estimate the size for
      Returns:
      the estimated length of the formatted string

    • justify

      public static String justify(String string, int length)
      Justifies to the right a string string to a specified length by prepending spaces if string is shorter than length. If string is longer than length, it truncates string to length.
      Parameters:
      string - the string to justify
      length - the desired length of the justified string
      Returns:
      the justified string

    • variation

      public static char variation(Object current, Object last)
      Determines the variation between two objects, current and last, assumed to be numbers. It returns VARIATION_UP if current is greater than last, VARIATION_DOWN if current is less than last, and VARIATION_SAME if they are equal. If either current or last is null, or if they are not instances of Number, it returns a space character.
      Parameters:
      current - the current value
      last - the last value
      Returns:
      a character representing the variation (↗, ↘, =, or space)
